extracted.intended_audience: FCC applicants, licensees, RF engineers, environmental consultants, and site owners/operators involved in antenna/ RF facility approval and compliance
extracted.subtask_short: FCC environmental and RF exposure compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory criteria and procedural requirements for evaluating and mitigating environmental impacts (including RF exposure) of proposed or existing FCC-regulated facilities, and for preparing Environmental Assessments (EAs) and Environmental Impact Statements (EISs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple RF sources exemption (≤1 mW and 2 cm separation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple RF sources are exempt if: (A) The available maximum time-averaged power of each source is no more than 1 mW and there is a separation distance of two centimeters between any portion of a radiating structure operating and the nearest portion of any other radiating structure in the same device, except if the sum of multiple sources is less than 1 mW during the time-averaging period, in which case they may be treated as a single source (separation is not required). This exemption may not be used in conjunction with other exemption criteria other than paragraph (b)(3)(i)(A). Medical implant devices may only use this exemption and that in paragraph (b)(3)(i)(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to multiple RF sources within the same device. If summed power <1 mW during averaging period, sources may be treated as single source and the 2 cm separation requirement may be waived. Cannot combine this exemption with other exemptions except as noted; medical implants limited to these exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple RF sources fractional-sum exemption (fractional contribution ≤1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple RF sources: in the case of fixed RF sources operating in the same time-averaging period, or of multiple mobile or portable RF sources within a device operating in the same time averaging period, if the sum of the fractional contributions to the applicable thresholds is less than or equal to 1 as indicated in the following equation. Where: a = number of fixed, mobile, or portable RF sources claiming exemption using paragraph (b)(3)(i)(B) for Pth; b = number ... (and definitions of Pi, Pth,i, ERPj, ERPth,j, Evaluatedk, Exposure Limitk are provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption is assessed by summing fractional contributions of each source to applicable thresholds using the specified variables and definitions (includes evaluated existing transmitters and those being added). Uses either available max time-averaged power or ERP (whichever greater) and incorporates existing evaluations, SAR/MPE values, and threshold ERPs per applicable formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation requirement for fixed RF sources
rubrics_metrics.description: As provided in paragraphs (b)(4)(ii) through (vi), specific mitigation actions are required for fixed RF sources to the extent necessary to ensure compliance with our exposure limits, including the implementation of an RF safety plan, restriction of access to those RF sources, and disclosure of spatial regions where exposure limits are exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation actions vary by category (Information, Notice, Caution, Warning/Danger) and include signage, access controls, training, time-averaging practices, PPE, and lockout/tagout where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category One — INFORMATION
rubrics_metrics.description: No mitigation actions are required when the RF source does not cause continuous or source-based time-averaged exposure in excess of the general population limit in § 1.1310. Optionally a green “INFORMATION” sign may offer information to those persons who might be approaching RF sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If used, the optional green INFORMATION sign must include at least: appropriate signal word 'INFORMATION' and color (green), an explanation of safety precautions to be observed when closer to the antenna than the information sign, reminder to obey postings and boundaries (if higher categories nearby), up-to-date licensee/operator contact information (if higher categories nearby), and a place to get additional information (e.g., a website if no higher categories nearby).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category Two — NOTICE
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigation actions are required in the form of signs and positive access control surrounding the boundary where the continuous exposure limit is exceeded for the general population, with the appropriate signal word 'NOTICE' and associated color (blue) on the signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs must contain the components in paragraph (b)(4)(vi). Under certain controlled conditions (e.g., restricted rooftop), a sign on the antenna may be sufficient if it specifies a minimum approach distance and is readable at that distance. Occupational personnel with access to these controlled areas must receive appropriate training; transient individuals must be supervised by trained personnel and time averaging may be required to ensure general population limits are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category Three — CAUTION
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs (with signal word 'CAUTION' and color yellow), controls, or indicators (e.g., chains, railings, contrasting paint, diagrams) are required (in addition to positive access control established for Category Two) surrounding the area in which the exposure limit for occupational personnel in a controlled environment is exceeded by no more than a factor of ten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs must contain components in paragraph (b)(4)(vi). If Category Two and Three signs would occupy same location, Category Two sign is optional. Where signs are not used, physical controls/indicators must mark the occupational exposure boundary. Training required for occupational personnel; transient individuals must be supervised. Time averaging is required for transient individuals; occupational personnel require six-minute time averaging for exposure reduction unless RF personal protective equipment (PPE) is properly used in lieu of time averaging. If power-reduction or category reduction is infeasible, lockout/tagout per 29 CFR 1910.147 must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category Four — WARNING/DANGER
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the occupational limit could be exceeded by a factor of more than ten, 'WARNING' signs (orange) and additional controls/indicators are required; 'DANGER' signs (red) are required where immediate and serious injury will occur on contact, in addition to positive access control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Category Three and Four boundaries overlap, Category Three sign is optional. No access is permitted without Category reduction. If power reduction/category reduction is not feasible, lockout/tagout procedures in 29 CFR 1910.147 must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: RF exposure advisory sign content and readability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: RF exposure advisory signs must be viewable and readable from the boundary where the applicable exposure limits are exceeded, pursuant to 29 CFR 1910.145, and include at least the following five components: (A) Appropriate signal word and color (DANGER/WARNING/CAUTION/NOTICE); (B) RF energy advisory symbol; (C) An explanation of the RF source; (D) Behavior necessary to comply with the exposure limits; and (E) Up-to-date contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs must be readable from locations required for compliance with exposure limits; specific signal words/colors are defined (DANGER red, WARNING orange, CAUTION yellow, NOTICE blue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared responsibility for compliance among licensees when multiple fixed RF sources exceed limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When the exposure limits in § 1.1310 are exceeded in an accessible area due to emissions from multiple fixed RF sources, actions necessary to bring the area into compliance or preparation of an EA are the shared responsibility of all licensees whose RF sources produce, at the area in question, levels that exceed 5% of the applicable exposure limit proportional to power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A licensee demonstrating its facility was not the most recently modified or newly-constructed facility establishes a rebuttable presumption that it should not be liable for the period of non-compliance. Field strengths must be squared to be proportional to SAR or power density. Site owners/managers should allow reasonable steps and encourage co-location/common solutions; applicants/licensees must share technical information necessary for joint compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA submission requirement for applicants causing >5% exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants (including renewal applicants) for proposed RF sources that would cause non-compliance with § 1.1310 at an accessible area previously in compliance must submit an Environmental Assessment (EA) if emissions from the applicant's RF source would produce levels at the area in question that exceed 5% of the applicable exposure limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field strengths must be squared where necessary to be proportional to SAR or power density. This applies to proposed and renewal applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interested person petition to require EA (allege significant environmental effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an interested person alleges that a particular action otherwise categorically excluded will have a significant environmental effect, the person shall electronically submit to the Bureau a written petition setting forth in detail the reasons justifying environmental consideration. If unable to submit electronically or if electronic filing is unreasonably burdensome, the petition may be mailed with a request for waiver under § 1.1304(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau shall review the petition and consider concerns raised; if the Bureau determines the action may have a significant environmental impact, the Bureau will require the applicant to prepare an EA (see §§ 1.1308 and 1.1311).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau-initiated EA and migratory bird note
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Bureau responsible for processing an action otherwise categorically excluded determines the proposal may have a significant environmental impact, the Bureau, on its own motion, shall require the applicant to electronically submit an EA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Pending final determinations regarding migratory birds, the Bureau shall require an EA for otherwise categorically excluded actions involving new or existing antenna structures requiring ASR (FCC Form 854) if the proposed antenna structure will be over 450 feet AGL and involves new construction, substantial increase in size, or addition of lighting/adoption of less preferred lighting style. EA required pursuant to this note is subject to the same procedures as other tower EAs per § 17.4(c) of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption of state/local regulation based on RF emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No State or local government or instrumentality may regulate the placement, construction, and modification of personal wireless service facilities on the basis of the environmental effects of radio frequency emissions to the extent such facilities comply with the FCC's RF environmental regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'personal wireless service', 'personal wireless service facilities', 'unlicensed wireless services', and 'direct-to-home satellite services' for purposes of the paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA purpose and review (what EA must accomplish)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants shall prepare EAs for actions that may have a significant environmental impact. The EA is a document which shall explain the environmental consequences of the proposal and set forth sufficient analysis for the Bureau or Commission to reach a determination that the proposal will or will not have a significant environmental effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau or Commission may request further information from applicants, interested persons, and agencies with jurisdiction or relevant expertise. For specified actions, the Commission shall solicit and consider comments of the Department of Interior, State Historic Preservation Officer, and Advisory Council on Historic Preservation, and consult tribes where actions affect tribal religious sites. See interagency cooperation references cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA outcomes and follow-up (finding of significant impact or FONSI)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Bureau/Commission determines, based on independent review of the EA and mandatory consultations, that the proposal will have a significant environmental impact, it will so inform the applicant, who may amend the application to reduce, minimize, or eliminate impacts. If the problem is not eliminated, the Bureau will publish in the Federal Register a Notice of Intent that EISs will be prepared. If the Bureau/Commission determines the proposal would not have a significant impact, it will make a finding of no significant impact and the applicant must provide community notice of the finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants have opportunity to amend; references to § 1.1308(c)-(d), § 1.1311, § 1.1314 and CEQ regulations (40 CFR 1501.4 and 1501.6) for community notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application amendment timing to address environmental concerns (§1.1309)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are permitted to amend their applications to reduce, minimize, or eliminate potential environmental problems. As a routine matter, an applicant will be permitted to amend its application within thirty (30) days after the Commission or Bureau informs the applicant that the proposal will have a significant impact upon the quality of the human environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments shall be made electronically. The 30-day period may be extended upon a showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAR limits and averaging times for occupational and general population exposures
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific absorption rate (SAR) shall be used to evaluate human exposure to RF radiation within 100 kHz to 6 GHz. Occupational/controlled SAR limits: 0.4 W/kg whole-body average; peak spatial-average SAR 8 W/kg averaged over any 1 gram of tissue; extremities peak spatial-average SAR 20 W/kg averaged over any 10 grams of tissue; exposure may be averaged over a time period not to exceed 6 minutes. General population/uncontrolled SAR limits: 0.08 W/kg whole-body average; peak spatial-average SAR 1.6 W/kg over 1 gram; extremities 4 W/kg over 10 grams; exposure may be averaged over a time period not to exceed 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These SAR limits apply for evaluation of environmental impact under § 1.1307(b). Exceptions: parts of the body treated as extremities have different peak spatial-average limits. Portable devices have specific SAR evaluation provisions under § 2.1093.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation methods and computational requirements for SAR compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation must demonstrate compliance with both whole-body and peak spatial-average SAR limits using technically supported measurement or computational methods and exposure conditions in advance of authorization, in a manner that facilitates independent assessment and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical computation of SAR must be supported by documentation showing the numerical method and software have been fully validated; equipment and exposure conditions must be modeled according to protocols established by FCC-accepted numerical computation standards or available FCC procedures. See OET Bulletin 65 and OET KDB for detailed procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of MPE limits and frequency applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: For operations within 300 kHz to 6 GHz, the limits for Maximum Permissible Exposure (MPE), derived from whole-body SAR limits and listed in Table 1, may be used instead of whole-body SAR limits (except for portable devices per § 2.1093). At operating frequencies above 6 GHz, the MPE limits in Table 1 must be used in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both MPE and SAR limits are for continuous exposure; higher exposure levels for shorter times are permitted provided the average over the specified averaging time is less than or equal to the limits. Refer to OET Bulletin 65 and FCC KDB for policies and evaluation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPE table values and definitions of occupational vs general population exposures (Table 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 sets forth MPE limits for electric field strength (V/m), magnetic field strength (A/m), and power density (mW/cm^2) for specified frequency ranges, with averaging times. Occupational/controlled exposure limits apply where persons are exposed as a consequence of employment and are 'fully aware' and can 'exercise control' over exposure; general population/uncontrolled exposure limits apply where the public may be exposed or persons may not be fully aware or able to exercise control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'fully aware' implies receipt of written/verbal information and, except for transients, appropriate training. 'Exercise control' means the person knows how to reduce or avoid exposure via administrative or engineering work practices (e.g., PPE, time averaging). Transient persons must be made aware and supervised where occupational limits apply and time averaging is used to ensure general population compliance. Example values in the table vary by frequency band (see § 1.1310(e)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: EA content requirements (what to include in an EA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EA shall contain the following information: (1) For antenna towers and satellite earth stations: a description of facilities/supporting structures and the site and surrounding area and uses (address impact of high-intensity white lighting in residential areas). (2) Statement of zoning classification of the site, communications with local/state/federal authorities and determinations. (3) Statement whether construction has been a source of controversy on environmental grounds. (4) Discussion of environmental and other considerations leading to site selection, nature/extent of unavoidable adverse effects, and any alternative sites or facilities reasonably considered. (5) Any other information requested by the Bureau or Commission. (6) If endangered/threatened species or critical habitats may be affected, analysis must utilize best scientific and commercial data available (see 50 CFR 402.14(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information must be factual (not argumentative), concise with sufficient detail to explain consequences and enable independent review. EA must address special environmental features (wilderness, preserves, migration paths, historic/archeological sites), specify effects on National Register-listed or eligible properties, detail substantial changes in land character (deforestation, wetland fill, water diversion), and discuss continuing patterns of human intrusion where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: EA supporting documentation and cross-referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: The EA shall be accompanied by evidence of site approval obtained from local or Federal land use authorities. To the extent information is submitted elsewhere in the application, it need not be duplicated in the EA but adequate cross-reference shall be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another federal agency has assumed responsibility for determining significant effects and invoking the EIS process, an EA to the Commission is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities without preconstruction authorization — applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: For facilities for which no Commission authorization prior to construction is required, the licensee/applicant shall initially ascertain whether the proposed facility may have a significant environmental impact or is categorically excluded. If it may have a significant impact, the information required by § 1.1311 shall be submitted electronically and ruled on by the Commission, and environmental processing shall be completed prior to initiation of construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility is categorically excluded, the licensee may proceed in accordance with licensing rules. If, after construction initiation, the licensee discovers the facility may have a significant effect, construction that may have that effect must cease and the EA submitted; processing must be completed before construction resumes. Paragraphs (a)-(d) do not apply to construction of mobile stations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections filing procedures based on environmental considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to applications (to which section 309(b) applies) based on environmental considerations must be filed electronically as petitions to deny. If the interested person is unable to file electronically or it is unreasonably burdensome, the petition may be submitted by mail with a request for waiver under § 1.1304(b). Informal objections based on environmental considerations must be filed electronically prior to grant of construction permit or authorization for facilities that do not require construction permits (or pursuant to rules for services subject to lotteries); again, mail filing may be allowed with a waiver request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing is the default; waivers for mail filing are allowed when electronic filing is impracticable or unduly burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS preparation triggers, scope, and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft and Final Environmental Impact Statements (DEISs and FEISs) shall be prepared by the Bureau when the Commission's/Bureau's analysis of the EA indicates the proposal will have a significant effect on the environment and the matter has not been resolved by amendment. The Bureau will publish a Notice of Intent to prepare EISs identifying the proposal, describing environmental issues, and inviting participation. EISs shall not address non-environmental considerations and should incorporate material by reference where feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau may request further information, direct technical studies, obtain expert opinion, and consult other agencies and authorities. The Bureau shall draft supplements to Statements where significant new circumstances/information arise. The Application, EA, DEIS, FEIS, and related documents and comments are part of the administrative record and must be filed electronically and made available for public inspection. Community notice and timing follow 40 CFR 1506.10 and guidance in 40 CFR part 1502.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEIS content and public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: The DEIS shall include: (1) A concise description of the proposal, the nature of the area affected, its uses, and any feature of special environmental significance; (2) An analysis of the proposal and reasonable alternatives exploring advantages/disadvantages and indicating direct and indirect effects and their significance for short- and long-term uses of the human environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a DEIS is prepared, the Commission files the Statement with the Office of Federal Activities, EPA, and public notice of availability is published in the Federal Register. Copies/summaries are electronically mailed to federal agencies with jurisdiction or expertise and to interested persons; hard copies/summaries must be provided by mail to those without electronic access. Any person or agency may comment on the DEIS within 45 days after notice of availability; comments must be filed electronically and mailed to the applicant per § 1.47.
